title: Yah Leh Monument

sources.facts: The national inscription archive measures the rectangular bronze plaque at 112 by 66 cm and 3 mm thick. It records one inscribed face with sixteen lines, an approximate Rama VI date, and a copper-alloy cast of the dog standing on a pedestal. It describes a rough coat, long ruff, dropped ears and a bushy tail.
The Tourism Authority identifies the standing life-size memorial before the castle and records the long coat, dropped ears and bushy tail of the dog.
The local authority records the metal statue, full scale and the royal verse mounted on its base.

notes: The photograph in Qualla has its photographer’s public-domain declaration. The status of the depicted sculpture was not independently established, so this original reconstruction instead uses the measured plaque, textual descriptions and exact named map point.
